rows.notes: Capchem board announcement 2024-017: Jingmen already had 80 kt/yr electrolyte capacity (phase I 60 kt, a technical upgrade of the original line, built and in production) and phase II adds 103 kt electrolyte (extended to 2026-12-31; the company says phase II will be pushed ahead as Central-China orders grow). The 28.3 万吨 project has three phases; phases I+II are electrolyte (6 + 10.3 万吨); the remaining ~12 万吨 (phase III) is not described as electrolyte in the opened sources and is excluded. capacity 183 kt = 80 kt existing + 103 kt phase II (both electrolyte); the 2026 step in capacity_by_year_json is the extended target date, not a confirmation. 2025 AR (S2) says phase II is still under construction at end-2025 and the 28.3 万吨 project EIA was re-approved 2025-11-13 (AR line 873-874). The 80 kt installed figure is as of the 2024-03-29 board date; later 2025 additions at Jingmen are not stated. Capchem company total (battery chemicals design capacity 681,577 t, AR 2025) is NOT split by the company.

Poland 40 kt/yr Li-ion electrolyte project went into formal production in April 2023 (Capchem Q3-2023 results call, via CLS; confirmed again by CLS 2024-05-21: 2023H1 production start). Phase 2 is only 'being prepared' per the 2025 annual report (S2) and its capacity is not stated (a Dec-2025 announcement gives investment <= RMB 200m per a search snippet, not opened). capacity_ref_year 2023 = date the 40 kt was built; phase 2 not added because no tonnage is sourced.

Dated and unattributed: CLS 2022-12-14 writes 'according to reports' that Capchem's Huizhou subsidiary had 35 kt/yr electrolyte and 50 kt/yr solvent capacity. This is a 2022 figure; the 2025 AR (S2 context, line 537) lists Huizhou phase-IV electronic-chemicals project as under construction (separate phase-4 200 kt row exists). Current Huizhou electrolyte capacity is probably higher but is not sourced; do not read 35 kt as 2025 capacity.

Mysteel 2026-01-27: Tinci's Xinhui District (Jiangmen, Guangdong) project (200 kt/yr electrolyte plus a 100 kt/yr battery-recycling part; construction began Dec 2022 per the article) 'has completed construction and begun operation'. The page names Tinci Materials, not the Jiangmen subsidiary; the match to this row is by location. installed 200 kt is the stated annual capacity at start-up (ramp-up not described). Tinci AR 2025 still lists the Jiangmen 20万吨 project as under construction at end-2025 (line 8223), consistent with a Jan-2026 start.

China Business Journal 2026-07-09 (and Jiemian, Nov 2026) state that the Liyang base 'now has 200 kt electrolyte capacity'. This matches the row's 200 kt project capacity. Company-level: Tinci AR 2025 lists lithium-ion battery materials design capacity 1,362,360 t (all materials, not electrolyte only) with ~1,000,000 t in construction (AR line 648); electrolyte sales 2025 >720 kt.

The task brief lists 'Ningde' and 'Fuding' separately; Fuding is under Ningde and no separate Ningde electrolyte site is sourced - treat as one base. Existing 200 kt is as of the article date. SEMCORP 2025 AR fundraising-project table: Jiangxi Tongrui '年产 4 亿平方米锂离子电池隔膜项目（一期）' (4 bn m2 = 400 Mm2, design date 2019-12-31) and the 'phase-I expansion' project are listed among projects that 'have reached production capacity (已达产)' but missed expected profit. 400 Mm2 is phase I only; the phase-I expansion (RMB 1.48bn) tonnage is NOT stated, so this is a lower bound for the site (and Jiangxi Enbo, Yichun, is a separate row). installed_as_of is the AR period end. The company total 14,400 Mm2 (AR 2025, line 435) is not split by the company.

SEMCORP 2025 AR: Suzhou Jieli '年产锂离子电池涂覆隔膜 2 亿平方米项目' (2 bn m2 = 200 Mm2 of COATED separator, fundraising project completed 2023-11-30) is listed as having reached production capacity (已达产). This is coating capacity on bought-in/own base film; it likely overlaps with base-film capacity at other SEMCORP sites and should not be added to the company's base-film total without checking.

Reported tier (page text garbled/mojibake, only the extracted statement is available): Hubei Enjie (Jingmen) is planned as a 16 bn m2 (1,600 Mm2) wet-process base-film and coated separator project, total investment RMB 5.2bn; SEMCORP is buying the 45% held by EVE for RMB 1.15bn (Sept 2026), so the EVE JV share in jv_partners may be outdated. 1,600 Mm2 is the planned total; installed capacity is not stated; the row is operational (existing). capacity_ref_year 2026 = publication fallback. Search for a cleaner source before relying on this.

Stockstar 2026-09-28: SEMCORP has acquired SK IE Technology's Jiangsu (Changzhou) plant; 'now has 8 base-film lines and 10 coating lines, design annual capacity 9.4 亿平方米' (940 Mm2, base film; coated output is not additive). The article says the business-registration change took effect 14 Sept 2026 (paraphrase from the fetch summary, not a verbatim quote), so the plant is now SEMCORP-owned; operator/parent fields were NOT changed here - lead to decide. Possible overlap: the existing row semcorp-jiangsu-changzhou-china (Jiangsu Enjie, Changzhou, a RMB 2.8bn EV separator project 'reached capacity' per the AR) may be a different plant in the same city; the sources do not say. The 2025 AR company total of 14,400 Mm2 predates the acquisition.

So the row's 300 kt is the full plan; installed phase-I tonnage is NOT stated in the AR (an unopened search summary suggests phase I = 200 kt - not used). Capacity fields left unchanged.

Shanshan 2025 AR: Meishan 20万吨 integrated base - phase I in production (一期已投产), phase II warehouse/dormitory under construction (二期仓库和宿舍在建中); 59.86% of the RMB 8bn budget (phase 1 = RMB 4.2bn). The row's 200 kt is the full plan; installed phase-I tonnage is not stated. Capacity fields unchanged.

Company total installed anode capacity is 250 kt at end-2025 (AR line 659-660; note 150 kt of graphitisation/carbonisation are largely outsourced per search snippets), i.e. below this single row's full plan. AR also states 2025 anode capacity additions of 12万吨 at Jiangsu/Tianjin/Sichuan/Huizhou/Shandong bases via technical upgrades, plus Indonesia phase II 8万吨 and Shenzhen 7,500 t silicon (AR lines 521-523) - not split by base, so Huizhou/Tianjin/Jiangsu/Jixi remain unallocated.
